kept.title: Command Injection via unsanitized branch arguments
kept.description: The `benchmarking/compare/index.js` file passes process arguments directly into `execSync` via the `exec` helper. An attacker controlling the arguments can inject arbitrary shell commands.
steps_to_exploit: Clone the repository.
Run `pnpm bench:compare 'branch; touch exploit.txt'`.
The shell executes `git checkout branch; touch exploit.txt`.
kept.impact: Remote Code Execution on the machine running the benchmarks.

evidence.quote: const checkout = is_jj ? (branch) => exec(`jj edit ${branch}`) : (branch) => exec(`git checkout ${branch}`);

code_refs.quote: const checkout = is_jj ? (branch) => exec(`jj edit ${branch}`) : (branch) => exec(`git checkout ${branch}`);

kept.title: Prototype Pollution via unflattened object keys
kept.description: In `src/parse.js`, the unflattening logic processes object keys but has incomplete protection against `__proto__` pollution when using custom object construction overrides.
steps_to_exploit: Construct a malformed JSON string payload targeting the unflattening logic.
Include a key named '__proto__'.
Observe that while the internal 'null' case blocks it, the standard 'else' block loop (lines 266-272) is vulnerable if the `ops.set` override is improperly implemented.
kept.impact: Global object pollution, potentially leading to privilege escalation or bypass of security controls in the host application.

kept.title: Denial of Service via unbounded recursion in hydrate
kept.description: The `hydrate` function in `src/parse.js` allows for deeply nested object structures without depth limits, potentially exhausting the call stack.
steps_to_exploit: Serialize a deeply nested array or object structure (e.g., 50,000 levels deep).
Pass the output to `devalue.parse()`.
The engine throws a RangeError: Maximum call stack size exceeded, crashing the process.
kept.impact: Application process crash leading to Denial of Service.

kept.title: Deserialization of untrusted input leads to arbitrary object creation
kept.description: The `parse` function does not validate the structure of the input array thoroughly, allowing an attacker to instantiate various types including URLs and Dates, leading to potential gadgets.
steps_to_exploit: Craft a payload defining arbitrary types supported by the reviver.
Trigger the `ops.fromStringValue` or constructor calls with malicious inputs.
Force the creation of objects that may cause side effects.
kept.impact: Creation of malicious object types during deserialization.

kept.title: Use of unsafe `eval`-like behavior in `uneval`
kept.description: The `uneval` function generates code that is then expected to be executed to recreate the value. While not using `eval()` directly, it produces code strings prone to scope capture issues.
steps_to_exploit: Pass an object with malicious keys that break out of the generated IIFE string.
The resulting string, when executed by a developer, runs attacker-controlled code.
kept.impact: Injection of arbitrary code when the output of `uneval` is executed.

kept.title: Denial of Service via large `length` properties in sparse arrays
kept.description: Although there is a check in `createSparseArray`, the `parse` logic relies on `is_valid_array_len` which trusts the `len` value provided in the serialized data.
steps_to_exploit: Provide a serialized array with a massive `len` property.
The `createSparseArray` implementation might attempt to allocate or set the length of a JS array.
Resulting in massive memory consumption.
kept.impact: Memory exhaustion and Denial of Service.

kept.title: Missing validation on `fromViewInfo` input
kept.description: The `parse` function uses `value[1]` as a buffer index without strictly checking that `value[1]` is a valid reference within the `values` array.
steps_to_exploit: Craft a malicious JSON payload where `value[1]` points to an index outside of `values` or points to an incompatible type.
The `fromViewInfo` operation will attempt to construct a view using a non-buffer type.
kept.impact: Unexpected runtime errors or type confusion in the target runtime.

kept.title: Insufficient validation of `ArrayBuffer` base64
kept.description: The `parse` function assumes `decode64(base64)` returns a valid buffer, but doesn't handle failures or malformed base64 strings gracefully.
steps_to_exploit: Send a payload with a non-base64 string in the ArrayBuffer slot.
The base64 decoder will throw an exception or return a corrupted buffer.

kept.title: Information leak via benchmark results file
kept.description: The `compare/index.js` script writes benchmark results into a file named after the branch. These files are saved in `.results/` and might contain sensitive info if the benchmarked code logs it.
steps_to_exploit: Run the benchmark on a branch that exposes environment variables.
Access the resulting JSON file in the `.results/` directory.
kept.impact: Unintentional exposure of sensitive build information.

kept.title: Unsafe `new Constructor()` calls with user-controlled strings
kept.description: In `parse.js`, the code uses `globalThis[tag]` where `tag` can be influenced by the input data.
steps_to_exploit: Provide a string in the payload that resolves to an unexpected global constructor (e.g., `Function`).
The parser calls the global constructor, potentially leading to code execution.
kept.impact: Potential arbitrary code execution if a dangerous constructor is allowed.

kept.title: Lack of output sanitization in benchmark console output
kept.description: The `compare/index.js` outputs branch names directly to the console group.
steps_to_exploit: Create a branch with a name containing ANSI escape sequences.
Run the benchmarking tool.
The console output will be manipulated by the ANSI codes.

kept.title: Insecure reliance on `Number.isInteger` for array indices
kept.description: Some index validation relies solely on `Number.isInteger`, which might fail to account for floating point edge cases in complex objects.
steps_to_exploit: Use extremely large numbers that are safe integers but might collide or behave unexpectedly.
The index logic might bypass boundary checks.
kept.impact: Data corruption or unintended behavior during deserialization.

kept.title: Potential prototype pollution via `__proto__` in `parse.js`
kept.description: While there is a check, `parse.js` performs a case-sensitive check for `__proto__`. Obfuscated variations might bypass it.
steps_to_exploit: Use a unicode representation or different casing if the environment allows it.
The parser might ignore the check and set the property.

kept.title: Insecure temporary files in benchmark directory
kept.description: The benchmark uses a predictable folder name `.results` for storing sensitive JSON output.
steps_to_exploit: Create a symlink to a sensitive file in the `.results` directory before the benchmark runs.
The benchmark overwrites the sensitive file.

kept.title: Use of `console.log` with user input
kept.description: The `benchmarking/run.js` script logs branch names and benchmark labels directly to console without sanitization.
steps_to_exploit: Inject malicious string payloads into benchmark labels.
The log will display the injected payload in the CI environment.
